script_structures: Set up the ordinary situation, then reveal the twist, then land the payoff.
Lead with a question the story answers by the end.
Open on a small detail, then zoom out to the bigger picture.
Set expectations early, then flip them in the back half.
Use a slow build with one big reveal near the very end.
Start in the middle of the action, then rewind to explain.
Contrast what you'd expect against what actually happened.

Introduce the normal expectation, then subvert it hard.
Build toward an 'and that's when it got weird' turn.

Structure it as three escalating moments, biggest last.
Build tension gradually across three beats, then release it in the last line.
phrasing_styles: Earnest, like you genuinely want the listener to feel what you felt.
Reflective, like you're still a little surprised by it yourself.
Casual but precise — no filler, but still sounds like a real conversation.
Direct eye-contact energy — like you're talking straight to one person.
Curious and searching, like you're figuring it out as you go.
Unhurried — let the details breathe before moving on.
Building excitement that peaks right at the reveal.
Grounded and matter-of-fact, letting the story's own weirdness do the work.
Slightly conspiratorial, like you're letting them in on something.
Confident storyteller voice — you already know how this ends and you're enjoying the telling.
Warm humor threaded through, without undercutting the actual point.
A little breathless, like you can't wait to get to the good part.
Intimate, like sharing something you don't tell everyone.
Conversational, like explaining it to a friend over coffee.
